headline: CORRESPONDENCE TO PARLIAMENTARY IMMUNITY LEVIED AGAINST JOAQÚN RAMÍREZ
content: According to Sergio Tejada, its appropriate to lift parliamentary immunity for Congressman Joaquín Ramírez. The official statement clarifies details about reports aired on Cuatro Poder and Canal N but does not confirm nor deny any investigation against congressman Joaquín Ramírez conducted by U.S.s Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA).  The DEA denies investigating presidential candidate Keiko Fujimori while remaining silent regarding investigations involving Congressmen Ramírez, who serves as General Secretary of Force Peru.   An official communication states that Ms. Fujimori has never been under DEA scrutiny. This response comes after allegations made during broadcasts where former pilot Jesús Velásquez claimed collaboration with the DEA led him to record conversations suggesting Mr. Ramírez received funds allegedly provided by Mrs. Fujimori for campaign purposes.  Meanwhile, the Prosecutor’s Office initiated procedures requesting information directly from the United States Anti-Narcotics Agency according to sources within Perú21. headline: KEIKO FJIMORI AND HER DEFENSE ON THE CHARGES
content: For us, what Lambert says publicly before cameras suffices, stated Gerardo Reyes, head investigator at Channel N. Meanwhile, leader of Force Peru, Keiko Fujimori again rejects claims broadcasted over Sunday programs stating she neither gave money to Ramírez nor was ever investigated by the DEA. She also mentioned meeting recently with the U.S. ambassador along with their delegation including two DEA agents, emphasizing nothing related to Ramírez was discussed.  She further explained how inquiries were requested through urgent letters addressed to the presidential hopeful representing Force Peru presented yesterday by lawmaker Hernán Béntez to said commission. headline: CRITICAL COMMENTS FROM FIRST LADY AND PREMIER REGARDING KEIKO FUJIMORIS CASE
